8b3fbdaaf8.substituent_description: A quinoline (ring N labelled N) carries, at C2 (the carbon adjacent to the ring N), an NH linker (N with H below) to a benzene ring that has a Me on the carbon ortho to the NH-bearing carbon (1,2-disubstituted). At C4 of the quinoline there is a C(=O)NHBn amide (C=O drawn as O with a double bond, then NHBn).
8b3fbdaaf8.notes: Typeset drawing. Quinoline drawn with Kekule double bonds (5 in the bicycle), tolyl ring 3, plus the amide C=O. The NH linker is written with H stacked below N.

cef9f795ec.substituent_description: Left benzene ring (drawn with an inner circle) has Cl on one carbon and, on a ring carbon separated from it by one ring carbon (meta, 1,3), a bond to the ring N of a five-membered ring N-N=C(NH-aryl)-NH-C(=O) (ring atoms N, C=O, NH, C, N: the C=O is flanked by the aryl-bearing N and an NH; the other carbon is double-bonded to the second ring N and carries an exocyclic NH, written N over H, leading to a second benzene ring). That second benzene (circle) has the NH at one carbon and CO2H at the opposite carbon (para).
overlaps_or_ambiguities: Hand-drawn left benzene ring is irregular and stretched, so the Cl versus ring-N attachment relationship was judged meta from vertex order and is slightly uncertain
Exocyclic NH written as N with H stacked below
cef9f795ec.notes: Handwritten. Double bonds: one C=O and one C=N in the five-membered ring. Both benzene rings are drawn as circles. CO2H written with a subscript 2 that is underlined.

1556a913f3.substituent_description: Left part is a carbazole-type tricycle (benzene circle, five-membered ring with N, second benzene circle) with Et on the ring N. The central benzene ring carries a CH2 on the carbon para to the carbon bonded to N, and that CH2 goes to the N of a piperidine whose carbon opposite the N is a spiro centre shared with a five-membered ring fused to a third benzene ring (circle). In the five-membered ring, the carbon next to the benzo ring bears NHAc on a hashed bond, and the carbon next to the spiro centre bears OH on a solid wedge.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: NHAc label has a stray stroke across the H
Aromatic rings are small irregular circles inside irregular hexagons
1556a913f3.notes: Handwritten. All three benzene-type rings are drawn with circles; no explicit double bonds. One solid wedge (to OH) and one hashed bond (to NHAc).

50310605c6.substituent_description: A spiro carbon joins an N-Boc pyrrolidine to a five-membered lactam ring (C=O next to the spiro carbon, lactam N) that is fused to a pyridine (ring N adjacent to the carbon bearing the lactam N; 7-azaoxindole type). The lactam N carries a CH2 to a benzene ring bearing OMe para to the CH2 (4-methoxybenzyl).
50310605c6.notes: Typeset drawing. Double bonds: lactam C=O (1), pyridine ring (3), methoxyphenyl ring (3).

743899565b.substituent_description: A six-membered ring with an inner circle and one ring N is fused to a five-membered ring containing an N bearing Ac. Going round the six-membered ring: fusion carbon bonded to N-Ac, CH, ring N, carbon bearing OMe (adjacent to the ring N), CH, fusion carbon bonded to the CH2 of the five-membered ring. The five-membered ring carbon next to N-Ac carries EtOOC.
743899565b.notes: Handwritten. Fused 6-5 bicycle (azaindoline type). Aromatic ring shown as a circle only, no explicit double bonds. Filled dots at some vertices are pen pressure, not charges.

015d4074cd.substituent_description: A benzene ring has EtOOC at one carbon and, para to it, a CH=C(CH3) alkene; the alkene carbon bearing a methyl is bonded to the aromatic ring of a tetrahydronaphthalene. That aromatic carbon is separated by one CH from the ring-fusion carbon attached to the top C(CH3)2; the saturated ring has two methyl stubs on each of the two carbons next to the aromatic ring (four methyls in total) and two CH2 between them.
015d4074cd.notes: Typeset drawing. Double bonds: alkene (1), benzene (3), tetralin aromatic ring (3). Methyls are drawn only as bond stubs: one on the alkene carbon and four on the tetralin ring. No E/Z label written.

ab90ded6b9.substituent_description: Left is a fused five/six bicycle (pyrrolo-pyrimidinone type): the five-membered ring N bears Me and the neighbouring carbon bears I; the six-membered ring contains N=CH, a substituted ring N and a C=O carbon. The ring N between the CH and the C=O carries a CH2 attached to C4 of a piperidine that also has HO on that carbon; the piperidine N is acylated by a C(=O) whose carbon is attached on a solid wedge to C4 of a second piperidine bearing N-Boc, with Ph on the adjacent C3 on a hashed bond.
ab90ded6b9.notes: Handwritten. Double bonds: C=N, ring C=O, fusion C=C, C=C next to C-I, and amide C=O. Rings: bicycle 5 and 6, then two piperidines. No stereo descriptors written.

6f62db5183.substituent_description: A long unbranched zigzag chain starting at Et runs to an NH that forms an amide C(=O) to a benzene ring; para to the amide, the ring carries a CH2CH2 chain attached to C4 of a piperidine. The piperidine N is part of a urea N-C(=O)-NH to a second benzene ring that carries an NMe2 group para to the urea NH.
6f62db5183.notes: Typeset drawing. Double bonds: two C=O (amide and urea) plus two benzene rings with 3 each. The chain between Et and NH has about ten zigzag vertices.
